Current CTM detection methods face two major barriers: complex measurement setups that are difficult to deploy in clinical or daily settings, and limited suitability for real-time application. The authors aim to address these challenges by developing a simple, wearable solution.
AI.method: Data were collected from 10 able-bodied participants performing activities of daily living under simulated impairment conditions (elbow brace restricting flexion-extension, resistance band inducing flexor-synergy-like patterns), with synchronized optical motion capture (OMC) and manually annotated video recordings as reference. A systematic location-reduction analysis identified wrist and trunk kinematics as a minimal sufficient set of anatomical sensing locations. An extreme gradient boosting classifier (XGBoost) with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation was used to evaluate a two-IMU model against an OMC-based model.
AI.result: The two-IMU model achieved strong discriminative performance (macro-F1 = 0.80 +/- 0.07, MCC = 0.73 +/- 0.08, ROC-AUC = 0.93+), with timing suitable for real-time applications. Explainability analysis showed trunk dynamics and wrist-trunk interaction features were the dominant contributors. In preliminary testing with four participants with neurological conditions, the model maintained good discriminative capability (ROC-AUC ~0.78), though performance was more variable and threshold-dependent.
AI.conclusion: Sparse wearable sensing using two IMUs is a viable pathway toward scalable, real-time monitoring of CTMs during therapy and daily living. The system achieves performance comparable to optical motion capture while being clinically practical. Future work should focus on improving generalization across clinical populations and standardizing evaluation protocols.

title: Habitat-GS: A High-Fidelity Navigation Simulator with Dynamic Gaussian Splatting
summary: Training embodied AI agents depends critically on the visual fidelity of simulation environments and the ability to model dynamic humans. Current simulators rely on mesh-based rasterization with limited visual realism, and their support for dynamic human avatars, where available, is constrained to mesh representations, hindering agent generalization to human-populated real-world scenarios. We present Habitat-GS, a navigation-centric embodied AI simulator extended from Habitat-Sim that integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting scene rendering and drivable gaussian avatars while maintaining full compatibility with the Habitat ecosystem. Our system implements a 3DGS renderer for real-time photorealistic rendering and supports scalable 3DGS asset import from diverse sources. For dynamic human modeling, we introduce a gaussian avatar module that enables each avatar to simultaneously serve as a photorealistic visual entity and an effective navigation obstacle, allowing agents to learn human-aware behaviors in realistic settings. Experiments on point-goal navigation demonstrate that agents trained on 3DGS scenes achieve stronger cross-domain generalization, with mixed-domain training being the most effective strategy. Evaluations on avatar-aware navigation further confirm that gaussian avatars enable effective human-aware navigation. Finally, performance benchmarks validate the system's scalability across varying scene complexity and avatar counts.

AI.tldr: Habitat-GS integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting for photorealistic rendering and gaussian avatars for dynamic human modeling, extending Habitat-Sim while maintaining full ecosystem compatibility.
AI.motivation: Training embodied AI agents depends on visual fidelity and dynamic human modeling. Current simulators use mesh-based rasterization with limited realism, and dynamic human avatars are constrained to mesh representations, hindering generalization to human-populated real-world scenarios.
AI.method: Extends Habitat-Sim with 3D Gaussian Splatting renderer for real-time photorealistic rendering and scalable 3DGS asset import. Introduces gaussian avatar module where each avatar serves simultaneously as a photorealistic visual entity and effective navigation obstacle.
AI.result: Agents trained on 3DGS scenes achieve stronger cross-domain generalization, with mixed-domain training being most effective. Gaussian avatars enable effective human-aware navigation. System scales effectively across varying scene complexity and avatar counts.
AI.conclusion: Integrating 3D Gaussian Splatting with gaussian avatars enables more realistic embodied AI simulation, leading to improved generalization and human-aware navigation capabilities.

title: Contextual Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Reef Monitoring
comment: To be published in IEEE OCEANS 2026 (Sanya) conference proceedings
summary: Although autonomous underwater vehicles promise the capability of marine ecosystem monitoring, their deployment is fundamentally limited by the difficulty of controlling vehicles under highly uncertain and non-stationary underwater dynamics. To address these challenges, we employ a data-driven reinforcement learning approach to compensate for unknown dynamics and task variations.Traditional single-task reinforcement learning has a tendency to overfit the training environment, thus, limit the long-term usefulness of the learnt policy. Hence, we propose to use a contextual multi-task reinforcement learning paradigm instead, allowing us to learn controllers that can be reused for various tasks, e.g., detecting oysters in one reef and detecting corals in another. We evaluate whether contextual multi-task reinforcement learning can efficiently learn robust and generalisable control policies for autonomous underwater reef monitoring. We train a single context-dependent policy that is able to solve multiple related monitoring tasks in a simulated reef environment in HoloOcean. In our experiments, we empirically evaluate the contextual policies regarding sample-efficiency, zero-shot generalisation to unseen tasks, and robustness to varying water currents. By utilising multi-task reinforcement learning, we aim to improve the training effectiveness, as well as the reusability of learnt policies to take a step towards more sustainable procedures in autonomous reef monitoring.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using contextual multi-task reinforcement learning for autonomous underwater vehicles to improve control in uncertain underwater environments, enabling policy reuse across different monitoring tasks.
AI.motivation: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are limited by controlling vehicles under highly uncertain and non-stationary underwater dynamics. Traditional single-task reinforcement learning overfits to training environments, limiting long-term usefulness of learned policies. The authors seek controllers that can be reused for various monitoring tasks, such as detecting different marine organisms in different reef environments.
AI.method: The authors employ a data-driven reinforcement learning approach using contextual multi-task reinforcement learning (MTRL) paradigm. They train a single context-dependent policy in a simulated reef environment (HoloOcean) that can solve multiple related monitoring tasks. The approach allows learning controllers that can be reused for various tasks.
AI.result: The contextual policies demonstrate: improved sample efficiency, zero-shot generalisation to unseen tasks, robustness to varying water currents, better training effectiveness, and improved reusability of learned policies compared to traditional single-task approaches.
AI.conclusion: Contextual multi-task reinforcement learning can efficiently learn robust and generalizable control policies for autonomous underwater reef monitoring, representing a step towards more sustainable procedures in marine monitoring by improving training effectiveness and policy reusability.

title: FeaXDrive: Feasibility-aware Trajectory-Centric Diffusion Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: End-to-end diffusion planning has shown strong potential for autonomous driving, but the physical feasibility of generated trajectories remains insufficiently addressed. In particular, generated trajectories may exhibit local geometric irregularities, violate trajectory-level kinematic constraints, or deviate from the drivable area, indicating that the commonly used noise-centric formulation in diffusion planning is not yet well aligned with the trajectory space where feasibility is more naturally characterized. To address this issue, we propose FeaXDrive, a feasibility-aware trajectory-centric diffusion planning method for end-to-end autonomous driving. The core idea is to treat the clean trajectory as the unified object for feasibility-aware modeling throughout the diffusion process. Built on this trajectory-centric formulation, FeaXDrive integrates adaptive curvature-constrained training to improve intrinsic geometric and kinematic feasibility, drivable-area guidance within reverse diffusion sampling to enhance consistency with the drivable area, and feasibility-aware GRPO post-training to further improve planning performance while balancing trajectory-space feasibility. Experiments on the NAVSIM benchmark show that FeaXDrive achieves strong closed-loop planning performance while substantially improving trajectory-space feasibility. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly modeling trajectory-space feasibility in end-to-end diffusion planning and provide a step toward more reliable and physically grounded autonomous driving planners.

AI.tldr: FeaXDrive addresses the insufficient physical feasibility of generated trajectories in end-to-end diffusion planning for autonomous driving by proposing a feasibility-aware trajectory-centric diffusion framework. It treats clean trajectories as the unified modeling object and integrates adaptive curvature-constrained training, drivable-area guidance, and feasibility-aware GRPO post-training to improve trajectory-space feasibility while maintaining strong closed-loop performance.
AI.motivation: Existing end-to-end diffusion planning methods use noise-centric formulations that are not well aligned with the trajectory space where feasibility is more naturally characterized, leading to local geometric irregularities, violation of kinematic constraints, and deviation from drivable areas.
AI.method: FeaXDrive proposes a trajectory-centric diffusion planning framework that models clean trajectories throughout the diffusion process. It incorporates three key components: (1) Adaptive curvature-constrained training to improve intrinsic geometric and kinematic feasibility; (2) Drivable-area guidance within reverse diffusion sampling to enhance consistency with drivable areas; (3) Feasibility-aware GRPO post-training to further improve planning performance while balancing trajectory-space feasibility.
AI.result: Experiments on the NAVSIM benchmark demonstrate that FeaXDrive achieves strong closed-loop planning performance while substantially improving trajectory-space feasibility compared to baseline methods.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of explicitly modeling trajectory-space feasibility in end-to-end diffusion planning, providing a step toward more reliable and physically grounded autonomous driving planners.

title: Reliability-Guided Depth Fusion for Glare-Resilient Navigation Costmaps
summary: Specular glare on reflective floors and glass surfaces frequently corrupts RGB-D depth measurements, producing holes and spikes that accumulate as persistent phantom obstacles in occupancy-grid costmaps. This paper proposes a glare-resilient costmap construction method based on explicit depth-reliability modeling. A lightweight Depth Reliability Map (DRM) estimator predicts per-pixel measurement trustworthiness under specular interference, and a Reliability-Guided Fusion (RGF) mechanism uses this signal to modulate occupancy updates before corrupted measurements are accumulated into the map. Experiments on a real mobile robotic platform equipped with an Intel RealSense D435 and a Jetson Orin Nano show that the proposed method substantially reduces false obstacle insertion and improves free-space preservation under real reflective-floor and glass-surface conditions, while introducing only modest computational overhead. These results indicate that treating glare as a measurement-reliability problem provides a practical and lightweight solution for improving costmap correctness and navigation robustness in safety-critical indoor environments.

AI.tldr: A lightweight method for constructing glare-resilient costmaps in mobile robotics that reduces false obstacles caused by specular glare on reflective surfaces.
AI.motivation: Specular glare on reflective floors and glass surfaces corrupts RGB-D depth measurements, creating holes and spikes that appear as persistent phantom obstacles in occupancy-grid costmaps, degrading navigation safety in indoor environments.
AI.method: A Depth Reliability Map (DRM) estimator predicts per-pixel measurement trustworthiness under specular interference, and a Reliability-Guided Fusion (RGF) mechanism modulates occupancy updates using this signal before corrupted measurements are accumulated into the map.
AI.result: The method substantially reduces false obstacle insertion and improves free-space preservation under real reflective-floor and glass-surface conditions, with only modest computational overhead on an Intel RealSense D435 and Jetson Orin Nano platform.
AI.conclusion: Treating glare as a measurement-reliability problem provides a practical and lightweight solution for improving costmap correctness and navigation robustness in safety-critical indoor environments.

title: Actuation space reduction to facilitate insightful shape matching in a novel reconfigurable tendon driven continuum manipulator
summary: In tendon driven continuum manipulators (TDCMs), reconfiguring the tendon routing enables tailored spatial deformation of the backbone. This work presents a design in which tendons can be rerouted either prior to or after actuation by actively rotating the individual spacer disks. Each disk rotation thus adds a degree of freedom to the actuation space, complicating the mapping from a desired backbone curve to the corresponding actuator inputs. However, when the backbone shape is projected into an intermediate space defined by curvature and torsion (C-T), patterns emerge that highlight which disks are most influential in achieving a global shape. This insight enables a simplified, sequential shape-matching strategy: first, the proximal and intermediate disks are rotated to approximate the global shape; then, the distal disks are adjusted to fine-tune the end-effector position with minimal impact on the overall shape. The proposed actuation framework offers a model-free alternative to conventional control approaches, bypassing the complexities of modeling reconfigurable TDCMs.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a model-free actuation framework for tendon-driven continuum manipulators with reconfigurable tendon routing, using curvature-torsion space projection and a sequential shape-matching strategy to simplify control.
AI.motivation: Reconfiguring tendon routing enables tailored spatial deformation of tendon-driven continuum manipulators (TDCMs), but actively rotating spacer disks adds degrees of freedom that complicate the mapping from desired backbone curves to actuator inputs.
AI.method: The authors project the backbone shape into curvature-torsion (C-T) space to identify which disks are most influential, then employ a sequential shape-matching strategy: first rotate proximal and intermediate disks to approximate the global shape, then adjust distal disks to fine-tune end-effector position with minimal impact on overall shape.
AI.result: The proposed framework provides a model-free alternative to conventional control approaches for reconfigurable TDCMs, significantly simplifying the control problem by leveraging geometric insights rather than complex modeling.
AI.conclusion: The C-T space projection and sequential shape-matching strategy enable effective control of reconfigurable TDCMs without the need for complex mathematical modeling, offering a practical solution for manipulating these devices.

title: VULCAN: Vision-Language-Model Enhanced Multi-Agent Cooperative Navigation for Indoor Fire-Disaster Response
summary: Indoor fire disasters pose severe challenges to autonomous search and rescue due to dense smoke, high temperatures, and dynamically evolving indoor environments. In such time-critical scenarios, multi-agent cooperative navigation is particularly useful, as it enables faster and broader exploration than single-agent approaches. However, existing multi-agent navigation systems are primarily vision-based and designed for benign indoor settings, leading to significant performance degradation under fire-driven dynamic conditions. In this paper, we present VULCAN, a multi-agent cooperative navigation framework based on multi-modal perception and vision-language models (VLMs), tailored for indoor fire disaster response. We extend the Habitat-Matterport3D benchmark by simulating physically realistic fire scenarios, including smoke diffusion, thermal hazards, and sensor degradation. We evaluate representative multi-agent cooperative navigation baselines under both normal and fire-driven environments. Our results reveal critical failure modes of existing methods in fire scenarios and underscore the necessity of robust perception and hazard-aware planning for reliable multi-agent search and rescue.

AI.tldr: VULCAN: A multi-agent cooperative navigation framework based on multi-modal perception and vision-language models for indoor fire disaster response, using physically realistic fire scenario simulations.
AI.motivation: Indoor fire disasters pose severe challenges due to dense smoke, high temperatures, and dynamically evolving environments. Existing multi-agent navigation systems are vision-based and designed for benign indoor settings, leading to significant performance degradation under fire-driven dynamic conditions.
AI.method: The authors extend the Habitat-Matterport3D benchmark by simulating physically realistic fire scenarios including smoke diffusion, thermal hazards, and sensor degradation. They introduce VULCAN, a multi-agent cooperative navigation framework based on multi-modal perception and vision-language models (VLMs) specifically tailored for indoor fire disaster response.
AI.result: Evaluating representative multi-agent cooperative navigation baselines under both normal and fire-driven environments reveals critical failure modes of existing methods in fire scenarios. The results demonstrate that current approaches struggle with fire-induced challenges, highlighting performance degradation when facing smoke, thermal hazards, and sensor degradation.
AI.conclusion: The study underscores the necessity of robust perception and hazard-aware planning for reliable multi-agent search and rescue in fire-driven dynamic environments, demonstrating that existing vision-based navigation systems are inadequate for the extreme conditions of indoor fire disasters.

title: GGD-SLAM: Monocular 3DGS SLAM Powered by Generalizable Motion Model for Dynamic Environments
summary: Visual SLAM algorithms achieve significant improvements through the exploration of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representations, particularly in generating high-fidelity dense maps. However, they depend on a static environment assumption and experience significant performance degradation in dynamic environments. This paper presents GGD-SLAM, a framework that employs a generalizable motion model to address the challenges of localization and dense mapping in dynamic environments - without predefined semantic annotations or depth input. Specifically, the proposed system employs a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queue to manage incoming frames, facilitating dynamic semantic feature extraction through a sequential attention mechanism. This is integrated with a dynamic feature enhancer to separate static and dynamic components. Additionally, to minimize dynamic distractors' impact on the static components, we devise a method to fill occluded areas via static information sampling and design a distractor-adaptive Structure Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) loss tailored for dynamic environments, significantly enhancing the system's resilience. Experiments conducted on real-world dynamic datasets demonstrate that the proposed system achieves state-of-the-art performance in camera pose estimation and dense reconstruction in dynamic scenes.

AI.tldr: GGD-SLAM is a visual SLAM framework that uses a generalizable motion model with FIFO queue and sequential attention to handle dynamic environments without semantic annotations or depth input, achieving state-of-the-art performance in pose estimation and dense reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Existing visual SLAM algorithms using 3D Gaussian Splatting rely on static environment assumptions and suffer significant performance degradation in dynamic scenes. There is a need for methods that can handle dynamic environments without requiring predefined semantic annotations or depth input.
AI.method: The system employs a generalizable motion model with a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queue to manage frames and a sequential attention mechanism for dynamic semantic feature extraction. It integrates a dynamic feature enhancer to separate static and dynamic components, uses static information sampling to fill occluded areas, and implements a distractor-adaptive Structure Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) loss tailored for dynamic environments.
AI.result: Experiments on real-world dynamic datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in camera pose estimation and dense reconstruction in dynamic scenes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed system significantly enhances resilience in dynamic environments without requiring semantic annotations or depth input, making it effective for visual SLAM applications in complex, changing scenes.

title: PAINT: Partner-Agnostic Intent-Aware Cooperative Transport with Legged Robots
summary: Collaborative transport requires robots to infer partner intent through physical interaction while maintaining stable loco-manipulation. This becomes particularly challenging in complex environments, where interaction signals are difficult to capture and model. We present PAINT, a lightweight yet efficient hierarchical learning framework for partner-agonistic intent-aware collaborative legged transport that infers partner intent directly from proprioceptive feedback. PAINT decouples intent understanding from terrain-robust locomotion: A high-level policy infers the partner interaction wrench using an intent estimator and a teacher-student training scheme, while a low-level locomotion backbone ensures robust execution. This enables lightweight deployment without external force-torque sensing or payload tracking. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate compliant cooperative transport across diverse terrains, payloads, and partners. Furthermore, we show that PAINT naturally scales to decentralized multi-robot transport and transfers across robot embodiments by swapping the underlying locomotion backbone. Our results suggest that proprioceptive signals in payload-coupled interaction provide a scalable interface for partner-agnostic intent-aware collaborative transport.

AI.tldr: PAINT is a lightweight hierarchical learning framework for collaborative legged transport that infers partner intent directly from proprioceptive feedback, decoupling intent understanding from terrain-robust locomotion without requiring external force-torque sensing or payload tracking.
AI.motivation: Collaborative transport requires robots to infer partner intent through physical interaction while maintaining stable loco-manipulation, which becomes particularly challenging in complex environments where interaction signals are difficult to capture and model.
AI.method: PAINT decouples intent understanding from terrain-robust locomotion using a hierarchical learning framework: a high-level policy infers partner interaction wrench via an intent estimator and teacher-student training scheme, while a low-level locomotion backbone ensures robust execution. This enables lightweight deployment without external force-torque sensing or payload tracking.
AI.result: Extensive simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate compliant cooperative transport across diverse terrains, payloads, and partners. PAINT naturally scales to decentralized multi-robot transport and transfers across robot embodiments by swapping the underlying locomotion backbone.
AI.conclusion: Proprioceptive signals in payload-coupled interaction provide a scalable interface for partner-agnostic intent-aware collaborative transport, enabling flexible deployment across different robots and environments.

title: Evolving the Complete Muscle: Efficient Morphology-Control Co-design for Musculoskeletal Locomotion
summary: Musculoskeletal robots offer intrinsic compliance and flexibility, providing a promising paradigm for versatile locomotion. However, existing research typically relies on models with fixed muscle physiological parameters. This static physical setting fails to accommodate the diverse dynamic demands of complex tasks, inherently limiting the robot's performance upper bound. In this work, we focus on the morphology and control co-design of musculoskeletal systems. Unlike previous studies that optimize single physiological attributes such as stiffness, we introduce a Complete Musculoskeletal Morphological Evolution Space that simultaneously evolves muscle strength, velocity, and stiffness. To overcome the exponential expansion of the exploration space caused by this comprehensive evolution, we propose Spectral Design Evolution (SDE), a high-efficiency co-optimization framework. By integrating a bilateral symmetry prior with Principal Component Analysis (PCA), SDE projects complex muscle parameters onto a low-dimensional spectral manifold, enabling efficient morphological exploration. Evaluated on the MyoSuite framework across four tasks (Walk, Stair, Hilly, and Rough terrains), our method demonstrates superior learning efficiency and locomotion stability compared to fixed-morphology and standard evolutionary baselines.

AI.tldr: A co-design framework (SDE) for musculoskeletal robots that evolves muscle strength, velocity, and stiffness simultaneously through spectral manifold projection with bilateral symmetry prior, achieving superior locomotion across diverse terrains.
AI.motivation: Existing musculoskeletal robot research relies on fixed muscle physiological parameters, which cannot accommodate diverse dynamic demands of complex tasks and limits performance upper bounds.
AI.method: Proposes Complete Musculoskeletal Morphological Evolution Space and Spectral Design Evolution (SDE) framework that integrates bilateral symmetry prior with PCA to project complex muscle parameters onto a low-dimensional spectral manifold, enabling efficient morphological exploration and co-design of morphology and control.
AI.result: Evaluated on MyoSuite framework across four tasks (Walk, Stair, Hilly, and Rough terrains), demonstrating superior learning efficiency and locomotion stability compared to fixed-morphology and standard evolutionary baselines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed SDE framework successfully enables efficient co-optimization of musculoskeletal morphology and control, overcoming the exponential exploration space problem and achieving better performance than fixed-parameter approaches.

title: OVAL: Open-Vocabulary Augmented Memory Model for Lifelong Object Goal Navigation
summary: Object Goal Navigation (ObjectNav) refers to an agent navigating to an object in an unseen environment, which is an ability often required in the accomplishment of complex tasks. While existing methods demonstrate proficiency in isolated single object navigation, their limitations emerge in the restricted applicability of lifelong memory representations, which ultimately hinders effective navigation toward continual targets over extended periods. To address this problem, we propose OVAL, a novel lifelong open-vocabulary memory framework, which enables efficient and precise execution of long-term navigation in semantically open tasks. Within this framework, we introduce memory descriptors to facilitate structured management of the memory model. Additionally, we propose a novel probability-based exploration strategy, utilizing a multi-value frontier scoring to enhance lifelong exploration efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed system.

AI.tldr: OVAL proposes a lifelong open-vocabulary memory framework for Object Goal Navigation, introducing memory descriptors for structured memory management and a probability-based exploration strategy with multi-value frontier scoring to enable efficient and precise long-term navigation in unseen environments.
AI.motivation: Existing ObjectNav methods excel at single-object navigation but have limitations in lifelong memory representations, hindering effective navigation toward continual targets over extended periods due to restricted applicability of memory systems.
AI.method: OVAL introduces (1) memory descriptors for structured memory model management, and (2) a novel probability-based exploration strategy using multi-value frontier scoring to enhance lifelong exploration efficiency.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed OVAL system for long-term navigation tasks.
AI.conclusion: OVAL enables efficient and precise execution of long-term navigation in semantically open tasks, overcoming limitations of existing methods through its lifelong open-vocabulary memory framework.

title: FastGrasp: Learning-based Whole-body Control method for Fast Dexterous Grasping with Mobile Manipulators
summary: Fast grasping is critical for mobile robots in logistics, manufacturing, and service applications. Existing methods face fundamental challenges in impact stabilization under high-speed motion, real-time whole-body coordination, and generalization across diverse objects and scenarios, limited by fixed bases, simple grippers, or slow tactile response capabilities. We propose \textbf{FastGrasp}, a learning-based framework that integrates grasp guidance, whole-body control, and tactile feedback for mobile fast grasping. Our two-stage reinforcement learning strategy first generates diverse grasp candidates via conditional variational autoencoder conditioned on object point clouds, then executes coordinated movements of mobile base, arm, and hand guided by optimal grasp selection. Tactile sensing enables real-time grasp adjustments to handle impact effects and object variations. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior grasping performance in both simulation and real-world scenarios, achieving robust manipulation across diverse object geometries through effective sim-to-real transfer.

AI.tldr: FastGrasp is a learning-based framework that enables mobile robots to perform fast grasping by integrating grasp guidance, whole-body control, and tactile feedback through a two-stage reinforcement learning approach (CVAE-based grasp candidate generation followed by optimal grasp selection and coordinated movement execution).
AI.motivation: Fast grasping is critical for mobile robots in logistics, manufacturing, and service applications. Existing methods face challenges in impact stabilization under high-speed motion, real-time whole-body coordination, and generalization across diverse objects and scenarios, limited by fixed bases, simple grippers, or slow tactile response capabilities.
AI.method: A two-stage reinforcement learning strategy: (1) A conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) generates diverse grasp candidates conditioned on object point clouds; (2) Optimal grasp selection guides coordinated movements of the mobile base, arm, and hand, with tactile sensing enabling real-time grasp adjustments to handle impact effects and object variations.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate superior grasping performance in both simulation and real-world scenarios, achieving robust manipulation across diverse object geometries through effective sim-to-real transfer.
AI.conclusion: FastGrasp effectively addresses the challenges of fast grasping for mobile robots by integrating grasp guidance, whole-body control, and tactile feedback, enabling robust manipulation across diverse objects and scenarios.

title: Frequency-aware Decomposition Learning for Sensorless Wrench Forecasting on a Vibration-rich Hydraulic Manipulator
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
summary: Force and torque (F/T) sensing is critical for robot-environment interaction, but physical F/T sensors impose constraints in size, cost, and fragility. To mitigate this, recent studies have estimated force/wrench sensorlessly from robot internal states. While existing methods generally target relatively slow interactions, tasks involving rapid interactions, such as grinding, can induce task-critical high-frequency vibrations, and estimation in such robotic settings remains underexplored. To address this gap, we propose a Frequency-aware Decomposition Network (FDN) for short-term forecasting of vibration-rich wrench from proprioceptive history. FDN predicts spectrally decomposed wrench with asymmetric deterministic and probabilistic heads, modeling the high-frequency residual as a learned conditional distribution. It further incorporates frequency-awareness to adaptively enhance input spectra with learned filtering and impose a frequency-band prior on the outputs. We pretrain FDN on a large-scale open-source robot dataset and transfer the learned proprioception-to-wrench representation to the downstream. On real-world grinding excavation data from a 6-DoF hydraulic manipulator and under a delayed estimation setting, FDN outperforms baseline estimators and forecasters in the high-frequency band and remains competitive in the low-frequency band. Transfer learning provides additional gains, suggesting the potential of large-scale pretraining and transfer learning for robotic wrench estimation. Code and data will be made available upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: A Frequency-aware Decomposition Network (FDN) for short-term wrench forecasting from proprioceptive history, designed for high-frequency vibration-rich interactions like grinding.
AI.motivation: Physical F/T sensors are limited in size, cost, and fragility. Existing sensorless estimation methods target slow interactions, but tasks involving rapid interactions (e.g., grinding) induce task-critical high-frequency vibrations where estimation remains underexplored.
AI.method: FDN predicts spectrally decomposed wrench with asymmetric deterministic and probabilistic heads, modeling high-frequency residuals as a learned conditional distribution. It incorporates frequency-awareness via adaptive input spectrum enhancement (learned filtering) and imposes a frequency-band prior on outputs. FDN is pretrained on a large-scale open-source dataset and transferred to downstream tasks.
AI.result: On real-world grinding excavation data from a 6-DoF hydraulic manipulator under delayed estimation, FDN outperforms baseline estimators and forecasters in the high-frequency band while remaining competitive in the low-frequency band. Transfer learning provides additional gains, demonstrating the potential of large-scale pretraining and transfer learning for robotic wrench estimation.
AI.conclusion: FDN effectively addresses the challenge of wrench estimation for vibration-rich, rapid interactions, showing superior high-frequency performance and competitive low-frequency performance. The results suggest that large-scale pretraining and transfer learning are promising approaches for robotic wrench estimation, with code and data to be released.

title: Robotic Manipulation is Vision-to-Geometry Mapping ($f(v) \rightarrow G$): Vision-Geometry Backbones over Language and Video Models
summary: At its core, robotic manipulation is a problem of vision-to-geometry mapping ($f(v) \rightarrow G$). Physical actions are fundamentally defined by geometric properties like 3D positions and spatial relationships. Consequently, we argue that the foundation for generalizable robotic control should be a vision-geometry backbone, rather than the widely adopted vision-language or video models. Conventional VLA and video-predictive models rely on backbones pretrained on large-scale 2D image-text or temporal pixel data. While effective, their representations are largely shaped by semantic concepts or 2D priors, which do not intrinsically align with the precise 3D geometric nature required for physical manipulation. Driven by this insight, we propose the Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model, which directly conditions action generation on pretrained native 3D representations. Specifically, VGA replaces conventional language or video backbones with a pretrained 3D world model, establishing a seamless vision-to-geometry mapping that translates visual inputs directly into physical actions. To further enhance geometric consistency, we introduce a Progressive Volumetric Modulation module and adopt a joint training strategy. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach. In simulation benchmarks, VGA outperforms top-tier VLA baselines including $π_{0.5}$ and GeoVLA, demonstrating its superiority in precise manipulation. More importantly, VGA exhibits remarkable zero-shot generalization to unseen viewpoints in real-world deployments, consistently outperforming $π_{0.5}$. These results highlight that operating on native 3D representations-rather than translating through language or 2D video priors-is a highly promising direction for achieving generalizable physical intelligence.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model, which replaces conventional language or video backbones with pretrained 3D representations to enable precise robotic manipulation and zero-shot generalization to unseen viewpoints.
AI.motivation: Robotic manipulation fundamentally requires vision-to-geometry mapping, but current VLA and video-predictive models rely on 2D image-text or temporal pixel data whose semantic/2D priors don't align with the 3D geometric nature of physical actions. The authors argue that a vision-geometry backbone is essential for generalizable control.
AI.method: VGA directly conditions action generation on pretrained native 3D representations using a 3D world model, introduces a Progressive Volumetric Modulation module for geometric consistency, and employs a joint training strategy to enhance performance.
AI.result: In simulation benchmarks, VGA outperforms top-tier VLA baselines (π₀.₅ and GeoVLA) in precise manipulation. More importantly, VGA demonstrates remarkable zero-shot generalization to unseen viewpoints in real-world deployments, consistently outperforming π₀.₅.
AI.conclusion: Operating on native 3D representations rather than translating through language or 2D video priors is a highly promising direction for achieving generalizable physical intelligence in robotic systems.

title: Tree Learning: A Multi-Skill Continual Learning Framework for Humanoid Robots
summary: As reinforcement learning for humanoid robots evolves from single-task to multi-skill paradigms, efficiently expanding new skills while avoiding catastrophic forgetting has become a key challenge in embodied intelligence. Existing approaches either rely on complex topology adjustments in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models or require training extremely large-scale models, making lightweight deployment difficult. To address this, we propose Tree Learning, a multi-skill continual learning framework for humanoid robots. The framework adopts a root-branch hierarchical parameter inheritance mechanism, providing motion priors for branch skills through parameter reuse to fundamentally prevent catastrophic forgetting. A multi-modal feedforward adaptation mechanism combining phase modulation and interpolation is designed to support both periodic and aperiodic motions. A task-level reward shaping strategy is also proposed to accelerate skill convergence. Unity-based simulation experiments show that, in contrast to simultaneous multi-task training, Tree Learning achieves higher rewards across various representative locomotion skills while maintaining a 100% skill retention rate, enabling seamless multi-skill switching and real-time interactive control. We further validate the performance and generalization capability of Tree Learning on two distinct Unity-simulated tasks: a Super Mario-inspired interactive scenario and autonomous navigation in a classical Chinese garden environment.

AI.tldr: Tree Learning is a multi-skill continual learning framework for humanoid robots that uses hierarchical parameter inheritance to prevent catastrophic forgetting, with multi-modal feedforward adaptation and task-level reward shaping, achieving higher rewards and 100% skill retention across various locomotion skills.
AI.motivation: As RL for humanoid robots evolves from single-task to multi-skill paradigms, efficiently expanding new skills while avoiding catastrophic forgetting has become a key challenge. Existing approaches either rely on complex topology adjustments in Mixture-of-Experts models or require training extremely large-scale models, making lightweight deployment difficult.
AI.method: Tree Learning adopts a root-branch hierarchical parameter inheritance mechanism providing motion priors through parameter reuse. A multi-modal feedforward adaptation mechanism combining phase modulation and interpolation is designed to support both periodic and aperiodic motions. A task-level reward shaping strategy is proposed to accelerate skill convergence.
AI.result: Unity-based simulation experiments show that compared to simultaneous multi-task training, Tree Learning achieves higher rewards across various representative locomotion skills while maintaining 100% skill retention rate, enabling seamless multi-skill switching and real-time interactive control. Performance and generalization are validated on a Super Mario-inspired interactive scenario and autonomous navigation in a classical Chinese garden environment.
AI.conclusion: Tree Learning effectively addresses the challenge of multi-skill continual learning for humanoid robots, preventing catastrophic forgetting while enabling seamless skill switching and real-time interaction.

title: E2E-Fly: An Integrated Training-to-Deployment System for End-to-End Quadrotor Autonomy
summary: Training and transferring learning-based policies for quadrotors from simulation to reality remains challenging due to inefficient visual rendering, physical modeling inaccuracies, unmodeled sensor discrepancies, and the absence of a unified platform integrating differentiable physics learning into end-to-end training. While recent work has demonstrated various end-to-end quadrotor control tasks, few systems provide a systematic, zero-shot transfer pipeline, hindering reproducibility and real-world deployment. To bridge this gap, we introduce E2E-Fly, an integrated framework featuring an agile quadrotor platform coupled with a full-stack training, validation, and deployment workflow. The training framework incorporates a high-performance simulator with support for differentiable physics learning and reinforcement learning, alongside structured reward design tailored to common quadrotor tasks. We further introduce a two-stage validation strategy using sim-to-sim transfer and hardware-in-the-loop testing, and deploy policies onto two physical quadrotor platforms via a dedicated low-level control interface and a comprehensive sim-to-real alignment methodology, encompassing system identification, domain randomization, latency compensation, and noise modeling. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to systematically unify differentiable physical learning with training, validation, and real-world deployment for quadrotors. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework for training six end-to-end control tasks and deploy them in the real world.

AI.tldr: E2E-Fly is the first unified framework that systematically integrates differentiable physics learning, reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer for end-to-end quadrotor control, featuring a full-stack training/validation/deployment workflow with two-stage validation and comprehensive alignment methodologies.
AI.motivation: Training and transferring learning-based quadrotor policies from simulation to reality faces challenges including inefficient visual rendering, physical modeling inaccuracies, unmodeled sensor discrepancies, and lack of a unified platform integrating differentiable physics learning into end-to-end training. Existing systems lack systematic, zero-shot transfer pipelines, hindering reproducibility and real-world deployment.
AI.method: Introduces E2E-Fly framework with: 1) Agile quadrotor platform; 2) High-performance simulator supporting differentiable physics and reinforcement learning; 3) Structured reward design for common tasks; 4) Two-stage validation (sim-to-sim transfer + hardware-in-the-loop testing); 5) Deployment via low-level control interface; 6) Comprehensive sim-to-real alignment including system identification, domain randomization, latency compensation, and noise modeling.
AI.result: Demonstrated effectiveness for training six end-to-end control tasks and successfully deployed them onto two physical quadrotor platforms.
AI.conclusion: First work to systematically unify differentiable physics learning with training, validation, and real-world deployment for quadrotors, providing a complete solution for sim-to-real control policies that bridges the gap between simulation and reality.

title: DINO-Explorer: Active Underwater Discovery via Ego-Motion Compensated Semantic Predictive Coding
summary: Marine ecosystem degradation necessitates continuous, scientifically selective underwater monitoring. However, most autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operate as passive data loggers, capturing exhaustive video for offline review and frequently missing transient events of high scientific value. Transitioning to active perception requires a causal, online signal that highlights significant phenomena while suppressing maneuver-induced visual changes. We propose DINO-Explorer, a novelty-aware perception framework driven by a continuous semantic surprise signal. Operating within the latent space of a frozen DINOv3 foundation model, it leverages a lightweight, action-conditioned recurrent predictor to anticipate short-horizon semantic evolution. An efference-copy-inspired module utilizes globally pooled optical flow to discount self-induced visual changes without suppressing genuine environmental novelty. We evaluate this signal on the downstream task of asynchronous event triage under variant telemetry constraints. Results demonstrate that DINO-Explorer provides a robust, bandwidth-efficient attention mechanism. At a fixed operating point, the system retains 78.8% of post-discovery human-reviewer consensus events with a 56.8% trigger confirmation rate, effectively surfacing mission-relevant phenomena. Crucially, ego-motion conditioning suppresses 45.5% of false positives relative to an uncompensated surprise signal baseline. In a replay-side Pareto ablation study, DINO-Explorer robustly dominates the validated peak F1 versus telemetry bandwidth frontier, reducing telemetry bandwidth by 48.2% at the selected operating point while maintaining a 62.2% peak F1 score, successfully concentrating data transmission around human-verified novelty events.

AI.tldr: DINO-Explorer is a novelty-aware perception framework for AUVs that uses semantic surprise signals and ego-motion conditioning to highlight significant underwater phenomena while suppressing self-induced visual changes, achieving 78.8% event retention with 48.2% bandwidth reduction.
AI.motivation: Marine ecosystem degradation requires continuous underwater monitoring, but most AUVs operate as passive data loggers capturing exhaustive video for offline review, missing transient high-value events. Active perception is needed with a causal, online signal that highlights significant phenomena while suppressing maneuver-induced visual changes.
AI.method: DINO-Explorer operates in the latent space of a frozen DINOv3 foundation model. It employs a lightweight, action-conditioned recurrent predictor to anticipate short-horizon semantic evolution, and an efference-copy-inspired module using globally pooled optical flow to discount self-induced visual changes without suppressing genuine environmental novelty.
AI.result: At a fixed operating point: 78.8% retention of human-reviewer consensus events, 56.8% trigger confirmation rate, 45.5% reduction in false positives, 48.2% bandwidth reduction, and 62.2% peak F1 score maintained.
AI.conclusion: DINO-Explorer provides a robust, bandwidth-efficient attention mechanism that effectively surfaces mission-relevant phenomena and concentrates data transmission around human-verified novelty events, dominating the validated peak F1 versus telemetry bandwidth frontier.

title: RMGS-SLAM: Real-time Multi-sensor Gaussian Splatting SLAM
summary: Real-time 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS)-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) in large-scale real-world environments remains challenging, as existing methods often struggle to jointly achieve low-latency pose estimation, 3D Gaussian reconstruction in step with incoming sensor streams, and long-term global consistency. In this paper, we present a tightly coupled LiDAR-Inertial-Visual (LIV) 3DGS-based SLAM framework for real-time pose estimation and photorealistic mapping in large-scale real-world scenes. The system executes state estimation and 3D Gaussian primitive initialization in parallel with global Gaussian optimization, thereby enabling continuous dense mapping. To improve Gaussian initialization quality and accelerate optimization convergence, we introduce a cascaded strategy that combines feed-forward predictions with voxel-based principal component analysis (voxel-PCA) geometric priors. To enhance global consistency in large scenes, we further perform loop closure directly on the optimized global Gaussian map by estimating loop constraints through Gaussian-based Generalized Iterative Closest Point (GICP) registration, followed by pose-graph optimization. In addition, we collected challenging large-scale looped outdoor SLAM sequences with hardware-synchronized LiDAR-camera-IMU and ground-truth trajectories to support realistic and comprehensive evaluation. Extensive experiments on both public datasets and our dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a strong balance among real-time efficiency, localization accuracy, and rendering quality across diverse and challenging real-world scenes.

AI.tldr: A tightly coupled LiDAR-Inertial-Visual 3DGS-based SLAM framework that enables real-time pose estimation and photorealistic mapping in large-scale scenes through parallel processing, cascaded initialization with voxel-PCA geometric priors, and Gaussian-based loop closure with pose-graph optimization.
AI.motivation: Real-time 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS)-based SLAM in large-scale real-world environments remains challenging because existing methods struggle to simultaneously achieve low-latency pose estimation, 3D Gaussian reconstruction step-by-step with incoming sensor streams, and long-term global consistency.
AI.method: The proposed framework implements a tightly coupled LiDAR-Inertial-Visual (LIV) system that executes state estimation and 3D Gaussian primitive initialization in parallel with global Gaussian optimization. It introduces a cascaded strategy combining feed-forward predictions with voxel-based principal component analysis (voxel-PCA) geometric priors for improved Gaussian initialization and accelerated optimization convergence. For global consistency, loop closure is performed directly on the optimized global Gaussian map using Gaussian-based Generalized Iterative Closest Point (GICP) registration followed by pose-graph optimization. The system uses hardware-synchronized LiDAR-camera-IMU sensors.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on both public datasets and a newly collected challenging large-scale looped outdoor SLAM dataset demonstrate that the method achieves a strong balance among real-time efficiency, localization accuracy, and rendering quality across diverse and challenging real-world scenes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach successfully addresses the key challenges of 3DGS-based SLAM by enabling continuous dense mapping through parallel processing, improving Gaussian initialization quality via cascaded strategies, and enhancing global consistency through Gaussian-based loop closure. The method provides a practical solution for real-time photorealistic mapping in large-scale environments.

title: XRZero-G0: Pushing the Frontier of Dexterous Robotic Manipulation with Interfaces, Quality and Ratios
summary: The acquisition of high-quality, action-aligned demonstration data remains a fundamental bottleneck in scaling foundation models for dexterous robot manipulation. Although robot-free human demonstrations (e.g., the UMI paradigm) offer a scalable alternative to traditional teleoperation, current systems are constrained by sub-optimal hardware ergonomics, open-loop workflows, and a lack of systematic data-mixing strategies. To address these limitations, we present XRZero-G0, a hardware-software co-designed system for embodied data collection and policy learning. The system features an ergonomic, virtual reality interface equipped with a top-view camera and dual specialized grippers to directly improve collection efficiency. To ensure dataset reliability, we propose a closed-loop collection, inspection, training, and evaluation pipeline for non-proprioceptive data. This workflow achieves an 85% data validity rate and establishes a transparent mechanism for quality control. Furthermore, we investigate the empirical scaling behaviors and optimal mixing ratios of robot-free data. Extensive experiments indicate that combining a minimal volume of real-robot data with large-scale robot-free data (e.g., a 10:1 ratio) achieves performance comparable to exclusively real-robot datasets, while reducing acquisition costs by a factor of twenty. Utilizing XRZero-G0, we construct a 2,000-hour robot-free dataset that enables zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer to a target physical robot, demonstrating a highly scalable methodology for generalized real-world manipulation.Our project repository: https://github.com/X-Square-Robot/XRZero-G0

AI.tldr: XRZero-G0 is a hardware-software co-designed system for scalable collection of high-quality action-aligned demonstration data in robot manipulation, using an ergonomic VR interface with dual grippers and a closed-loop data pipeline that enables combining minimal real-robot data with large-scale robot-free data at a 10:1 ratio to achieve comparable performance while reducing acquisition costs by 20x.
AI.motivation: The acquisition of high-quality, action-aligned demonstration data is a fundamental bottleneck for scaling foundation models in dexterous robot manipulation. While robot-free human demonstrations (e.g., UMI paradigm) offer a scalable alternative to traditional teleoperation, current systems suffer from sub-optimal hardware ergonomics, open-loop workflows, and lack of systematic data-mixing strategies.
AI.method: XRZero-G0 features an ergonomic virtual reality interface equipped with a top-view camera and dual specialized grippers for improved collection efficiency. It implements a closed-loop collection, inspection, training, and evaluation pipeline for non-proprioceptive data that achieves an 85% data validity rate. The system empirically investigates scaling behaviors and optimal mixing ratios of robot-free data, and constructs a 2,000-hour robot-free dataset.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that combining a minimal volume of real-robot data with large-scale robot-free data at a 10:1 ratio achieves performance comparable to exclusively real-robot datasets while reducing acquisition costs by a factor of twenty. The system enables zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer to target physical robots.
AI.conclusion: XRZero-G0 establishes a highly scalable methodology for generalized real-world manipulation through its hardware-software co-design approach, closed-loop quality control pipeline achieving 85% validity rate, and data-mixing strategy that significantly reduces acquisition costs without sacrificing performance.

title: Learning Versatile Humanoid Manipulation with Touch Dreaming
summary: Humanoid robots promise general-purpose assistance, yet real-world humanoid loco-manipulation remains challenging because it requires whole-body stability, dexterous hands, and contact-aware perception under frequent contact changes. In this work, we study dexterous, contact-rich humanoid loco-manipulation. We first develop an RL-based whole-body controller that provides stable lower-body and torso execution during complex manipulation. Built on this controller, we develop a whole-body humanoid data collection system that combines VR-based teleoperation with human-to-humanoid motion mapping, enabling efficient collection of real-world demonstrations. We then propose Humanoid Transformer with Touch Dreaming (HTD), a multimodal encoder--decoder Transformer that models touch as a core modality alongside multi-view vision and proprioception. HTD is trained in a single stage with behavioral cloning augmented by touch dreaming: in addition to predicting action chunks, the policy predicts future hand-joint forces and future tactile latents, encouraging the shared Transformer trunk to learn contact-aware representations for dexterous interaction. Across five contact-rich tasks, Insert-T, Book Organization, Towel Folding, Cat Litter Scooping, and Tea Serving, HTD achieves a 90.9% relative improvement in average success rate over the stronger baseline. Ablation results further show that latent-space tactile prediction is more effective than raw tactile prediction, yielding a 30% relative gain in success rate. These results demonstrate that combining robust whole-body execution, scalable humanoid data collection, and predictive touch-centered learning enables versatile, high-dexterity humanoid manipulation in the real world. Project webpage: humanoid-touch-dream.github.io.

AI.tldr: HTD (Humanoid Transformer with Touch Dreaming) is a multimodal Transformer that learns contact-aware representations for dexterous humanoid manipulation by predicting future tactile latents alongside actions, achieving 90.9% relative improvement in success rates across five contact-rich tasks.
AI.motivation: Real-world humanoid loco-manipulation is challenging because it requires whole-body stability, dexterous hands, and contact-aware perception under frequent contact changes, and current approaches lack the ability to effectively model touch as a core modality.
AI.method: The authors developed (1) an RL-based whole-body controller for stable lower-body and torso execution, (2) a VR-based teleoperation data collection system with human-to-humanoid motion mapping, and (3) HTD, a multimodal encoder-decoder Transformer trained with behavioral cloning augmented by touch dreaming that predicts action chunks, hand-joint forces, and tactile latents simultaneously.
AI.result: Across five contact-rich tasks (Insert-T, Book Organization, Towel Folding, Cat Litter Scooping, Tea Serving), HTD achieved a 90.9% relative improvement in average success rate over a stronger baseline. Ablation studies showed latent-space tactile prediction was 30% more effective than raw tactile prediction.
AI.conclusion: Combining robust whole-body execution, scalable humanoid data collection via VR teleoperation, and predictive touch-centered learning enables versatile, high-dexterity humanoid manipulation in real-world contact-rich scenarios.
